object: Oblong altar, 40 cm. × 32 cm., including short spout, field sunk and narrow spout-channel.
lines_described: One to two lines of late transitional writing round the border.
first: (1)wosi : sori(2)yi : slotoyemywi : (3)metelstowo(sic) : ñaye : te(4)dḫeli : tedḫelowi ato (5)mẖe psimte at (6)mẖe psiḫrke(7)too : ḫmlol : mol : ate
final: (1)wosi : sori(2)yi : mlotoyeqowi : (3)metelẖtowo(sic) : mnye : te(4)dḫeli : tedḫelowi ato (5)mẖe psimte at (6)mẖe psiḫrke(7)too : ḫmlol : ẖol : kete
rendering: O Wêsh! O Ashêri! Malêtêye : belonging to the great mate : truly born of Manaye. (Formulae A B C.)

changes.why: First 3-shaped sign is m (Malêtêye = m-l-o-to-y-e). The group '3-shape with tail + two strokes' before -wi is the same group Griffith reads qê in No. 20 (qêrezek), so q + o, not m + y.
His rendering 'the great mate' = mte + lẖ (great); his alternative 'the matelash' would keep s.
Manaye = m-n-y-e: the 3-loop with long tail to lower left is m, the 2-shape with long tail is n (not ñ + a).
p. 600 (formula C): 'n° 19 divides ẖêl : kete'.
Same note; the '52'-looking group is k (2 with long tail) + e, the a / e + k trap of the hand key.

kept.why: The copy clearly has the e sign (flat-topped 5) between m and te; his English would print 'mete' if he read it.
Copy shows to (ب with dot below) + o-stroke at the start of part 7; kept as drawn.

unsure.why: 3-shaped sign + two strokes; Griffith renders only 'Malêtêye' and leaves the suffix out.
3-shaped sign; Griffith gives both 'great mate' (lẖ) and 'matelash' (ls).

unsure.could_be: a variant ending of formula B (p. 600 says the final word is very variable)
unsure.why: Unusual ending; signs are clear in the copy.
3-shaped; his note p. 647 lists No. 19 among the texts with mte for ẖte, so m kept.

notes: Altar: the raised numbers mark parts of the border text. Order: row 1 right (parts 1-2), row 1 left (rest of 2), row 2 right (3), row 2 left (3 cont., 4), then rows 3, 4, 5 = formulae A (ato mẖe psimte), B (at mẖe psiḫrke) and C (ḫmlol : ẖol : kete), parts 5-7. 'sic' is printed over the o-stroke at the end of metelẖtowo. No divider between tedḫelowi and ato, nor between psimte and at. Griffith: the name is much rubbed. Spaces between formula words follow word division, not always a clear gap in the copy.

object: Altar broken in half and spout gone, 51 cm. 5 × 45 cm.
lines_described: Two to three lines of transitional writing round the border
first: (1)wosi : soreyi : nwteyẖy : sde(2)sdeselo : ẖyredlklo : yite(3)lito : ldesdeselo : wibik(4)ror : erikelo : wosi : sore(5)yi : (6)aḫ(7)ẖlo(8)li : (9)ẖol(10)k?[.][.]
final: (1)wosi : soreyi : nwteyqo : sde(2)mdeselo : qoredeklo : yilo(3)lise : tdemdeselo : wibik(4)ror : erikelo : wosi : sore(5)yi : (6)aḫ(7)ẖlo(8)li : (9)ẖol(10)k?[.][.]
rendering: O Wêsh! O Ashêri! Nawateya : shaze-mazes : qêrezèk : yilêlis : taze-mazes : begotten of Wibikarêr. O Wèsh! O Ashèri! (Formula D 2.)

changes.why: The last group (3 with closed loop + two strokes) is identical to the group Griffith reads qê at the start of qêrezek.
shaze-mazes: second 3-shaped sign is m.
qêrezek (note p. 580): stroke + 3 = q, stroke = o; the S-shaped sign before k is e, not l.
yilêlis: the unbarred /ϟ is lo, not te; last sign (ب-like with one stroke) is se ('s').
taze-mazes: first sign t, 3-shaped sign m.

kept.why: The final group is drawn exactly like the qê of qêrezek two words later; the copy shows no a sign.
The copy has the o-stroke (/), not the e sign.

unsure.why: S-curve with long stroke and no dot; t only on Griffith's 'taze'.
ب-like sign with a single stroke below, unlike the V + two strokes of se in mazes.

unsure.could_be: one lost sign if the k body lies under the hatching
unsure.why: Only the long tail of k is drawn; hatching about two sign widths; text broken off.
The note on p. 580 prints qêrezek with plain e; the copy sign is S-shaped.

notes: Order: row 1 right, row 1 left, row 2 right (part 2), row 2 left, row 3 right (3), row 3 middle, row 3 left (4), row 4 (repeated invocation, part 5, then formula D2 parts 6-10, broken off in hatching). Each epithet ends in -lo (unbarred /ϟ), which Griffith leaves out of the English but prints in his Kar. 80 parallel (szemzeslê). In the rendering 'qêrezèk', 'Wèsh' and 'Ashèri' are printed with a grave-like accent, probably damaged circumflexes. Griffith's footnote: description from notes at discovery; photograph lost. Dots under some signs in rows 2-3 not read as signs.

rendering: O Wêsh! O Ashêri! Khalalacharêr: born of Arekhatake: begotten of . . . eqetame : great shamat : great qêreñ : prophet of Amanap in Bezewi : peshatê in Akiñ : wayekite (?) in Amêz : wayekite-witakaw shêr in Zalitawaketiyi : yireke of akilikaw Charimali : yitebereke satani yiwazake : malê of mañake. O Wêsh! O Ashêri! (Formulae C A.) shakhêl qeshatani ye. . . : arezetani are of makhêbaral kezekazi : malê of the king (?) : malê of the god (?) : malê of the shalakh. tereki takabache of the akhararab, in Taketêre, and of the akhararab, in Amêz : qetezeli in Yezeyake.

changes.why: Khalalacharêr: first 3-shaped sign ẖ; the small H-like sign is l.
Arekhatake: 3-shaped sign is ẖ.
eqetame: hooked first sign e, 3-shaped sign m.
qêreñ: the loop-and-stroke sign is ñ here.
Akiñ.
wayekite (?): on closer crop the hatching holds traces of 4 (i) and a barred ϟ, with the te stroke clear.
Amêz (twice, rows 5 and 13): 3-shaped sign m.
Zalitawaketiyi: the first of the two H-like signs is l.
Charimali: 3-shaped sign m.
malê of mañake: m, ñ.
shakhêl: the stroke + 3 group is ẖ + o, not q.
malê (three times), the god (mk), shalakh (slẖ).
akhararab: 3-shaped sign ẖ.

kept.why: The copy has the o-stroke after r and the barred te sign, not e and t.
The copy has a single 4-sign with a long crossbar; where this engraver writes yi he draws strokes + 4 (yiwdkelo, yirekelo).
Copy shows barred te then one 4-sign, no y.
Copy has dividers inside ant and no a before mnp.
In the copy the clear e sign stands to the right (read first) of the hatched strokes.
No e between k and te in the copy.

unsure.why: Hatching about one sign wide before the divider; Griffith's name ends -charêr.

unsure.why: Hatched blob, about one and a half sign widths.

unsure.read: about four lost signs, then e?
unsure.why: Long hatching; first visible sign hooked (Griffith e).
Hatched signs and a tall stroke after k; Griffith 'begotten of'.
4 + hook groups read li; Griffith leaves these suffixes out of the English.
Hatched; n from his 'satani'.
Hatched; from 'qeshatani'.
Stroke + 3 group; Griffith makhêbaral.
Hatched 3-shaped sign; Griffith shalakh.
Hatched S-shape; t from his 'Taketêre'.
Hatched, nothing readable.

Hand-key trap q against ẖ + o; his shakhêl decides.

notes: Order follows the raised numbers: rows 1-9 are the border text (parts 1-21), each row read right part, (middle), then left part; row 9 holds the repeated invocation and formulae C (ḫmlol : ẖolkte) and A (ato mẖe : iẖte). Rows 10-12 (parts 22-25) and 13-15 (parts 26-29) are the two field texts on either side of the amphora; Griffith's English reorders the field texts (e.g. 'tereki takabache of the akhararab, in Taketêre' = rows 13-14). 'Bezewi' in his English spells be-ze-wi, matching the copy's bedewi. The '-lo' / '-li' suffixes are omitted in his English. The odd mark after 'Khalalacharêr:' in the print is a blemish. I glimpsed his notes on No. 21 (p. 620: Bezewi, wayekite, shêr, Charimali, yireke, Amenap) while reading No. 20's notes, before reading this copy, so 'first' is not fully blind for those words; I also knew the formula notes on pp. 647-648 from No. 19.

object: Square altar, 31 cm. × 39 cm., including spout, field and spout-channel sunk leaving in relief a jar between four circular loaves.
lines_described: One to two lines of late writing on border.
first: (1)w?osi (2)sore(3)yi : aderolo(4)wi : tepedeyi ted(5)ḫeli tedḫ[.]lo(6)wi? : ato (7)mẖe piskte at (8)mẖe pisiḫr
final: (1)w?osi (2)sore(3)yi : aderolo(4)wi : tepedeyi ted(5)ḫeli tedḫ[.]lo(6)wi? : ato (7)mẖe pismte at (8)mẖe pisiḫr
rendering: O Wêsh! O Ashêri! Azerê : truly born of Tepezeyi. (Formulae AB.)

changes.why: p. 647: n° 22 has mte for ẖte; the Ʒ-shaped sign with long bar is m here.

unsure.why: Drawn as a dotted outline (trace).
Hatching between ḫ and l (tedḫelowi); final i only a dotted outline.
Ʒ-shape with a long crossbar.

notes: Order: row 1 right (parts 1-3), row 1 left (4: Azerê), row 2 right (Tepezeyi, no number), row 2 middle (5: tedḫeli), row 2 left (6: tedḫelowi), row 3 (7: formula A), row 4 (8: formula B, ending at r where Griffith writes 'end'). Lines in the copy join the end of one row to the next. Griffith's 'truly born of' = tedḫeli tedḫelowi (as in No. 19). Contamination: I saw this text's description and rendering on p. 624 (while reading the end of No. 21's notes) before reading the copy, so 'first' is not blind.

object: Oblong altar, 43 cm. × 39 cm., including spout.
lines_described: One line of late inscription round the border.
first: (1)wosi sore(2)yi as?yesywi (3)tekeyewi terikelowi (4)tewinye tedḫelowi ato : mẖe psom?(sic)(5)[.]kete at mẖe psḫrkete (6)ḫmlol : pẖolkete
final: (1)wosi sore(2)yi kes?yeqowi (3)tekeyewi terikelowi (4)tewiñye tedḫelowi ato : mẖe psom?(sic)(5)[.]kete at mẖe psḫrkete (6)ḫmlol : pẖolkete
rendering: O Wêsh! O Ashêri! Keshaye : begotten of Tekeyewi : born of Tewiñaye. (Formulae A B C.)

changes.why: Keshaye: the '52' with long tail is k + e (hand-key trap); the 3-shape + two strokes before -wi is q + o (as qê in No. 20).
Tewiñaye: the loop sign with long tail is ñ.

unsure.why: Griffith prints ? above this 3-shaped sign; s from 'Keshaye'.

unsure.could_be: ẖ for m; the hatched sign unreadable
unsure.why: Griffith prints 'sic?' over this part of formula A; the third word is irregular.
Suffix not rendered by Griffith; same group as No. 19.

notes: Order: row 1 right (1-2: invocation, no dividers), row 1 left (Keshaye), row 2 right (3: Tekeyewi), row 2 left (terikelowi), row 3 right (4: Tewiñaye), row 3 left (tedḫelowi), row 4 (formula A, ato : mẖe separated as Griffith notes p. 647, part 5 inside the third word), row 5 (formula B), row 6 (6: formula C, phêl as noted p. 648). Long lines in the copy join row ends to the next row. I saw this text's description (p. 624) before the copy, not its rendering.
